SS2 is a Direct3D title (d3d124 in lanparty_titles.json). .124 runs the experimental vcr-kmd driver on its V5 6000, so it was not launched. SS2 has rendered its menu there before (2026-09-29, 2026-11-08), but only in supervised sessions.

boxes.reason: Windows 7 with the GTX 1650 on the Standard VGA stub, so there is no 3D driver. It also has no disc mounter for the SafeDisc v1 check.
boxes.evidence: Not in the title's boxes list, and the gate suppresses the shortcut.

boxes.reason: Win98 P166 is below the title's CPU floor; its Voodoo 2 does Glide only, not D3D; and it has no disc mounter.
boxes.evidence: The title is not installed there (operator override 'not wanted on .243'). Not touched.

summary: System Shock 2 is single-player only as staged (retail Final 1.15, no multiplayer patch on the share, no server). I re-verified it now on all 7 applicable XP boxes (.110 .123 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240). On each one the SafeDisc v1 disc-mount launch passed: SHOCK2.ICD was running, the LookingGlass game shell window had the foreground, the display was in a 640x480x16 fullscreen mode, and the TRI.OPTIMUM main menu was rendered, so all 7 are PASS_SP. This is the first time it has been seen rendering on .110, .123, .184 and .240. .124 is BLOCKED (D3D on vcr-kmd is supervised-only). .186 and .243 are NA. Games closed and every box is back at its desktop mode.
issues: lanparty kill had to force-close shock2.exe/SHOCK2.ICD on all 7 boxes, because WM_CLOSE was ignored for 12 s. The recipe warns that an unclean exit can leave the DAEMON Tools unit 'locked', which only a reboot clears. This cannot be read remotely, so on the next SS2 launch watch for a 'Unit is locked' dialog or 'Cannot locate the CD-ROM'.
The menu is a 2D panel, so this proves the launch, the copy protection and the fullscreen mode but not the 3D renderer (New Game was not started). .133 has rendered 3D in-game in an earlier session.
lanparty kill takes the game as a positional argument (kill SystemShock2), not --game, so the task's command line is wrong.

lanparty's frames are SCREENSHOT 1 at 320x240, and some boxes produced byte-identical images (.110 = .240, .123 = .184) because the menu is static. Each box's own WINLIST and DISPLAYCFG from the same minute tie the frame to that box.
